title: Robots.txt Guard
summary: Catches robots.txt rules that would quietly de-index a site, like Disallow: / in production or blocked CSS and JS.
description: robots.txt checker that flags Disallow: / for production, staging leftovers, rules blocking CSS/JS Google renders with, relative or wrong-host sitemaps, typos and fields Google ignores, with one-tap fixes and a URL tester naming the deciding line.
catches: Disallow: / and staging leftovers in a production file
Rules that block CSS and JS asset paths used for rendering
Which line decides a crawl for a given URL and user agent
limits: Models Google's robots.txt rules; other crawlers interpret files differently
robots.txt controls crawling, not indexing; blocked URLs can still be indexed from links
Asset checks use the paths you pass
a11y: Visible <label> on the textarea; aria-invalid on errors and a role=status issue count
Each issue has a button to select its line, with an aria-label
After a fix, focus moves to the next fix or back to the textarea
URL tester inputs have labels; results use icon plus text

sources.label: Google Search Central – How Google interprets the robots.txt specification

rules.note: Confirmed: Google supports user-agent, allow, disallow and sitemap (crawl-delay isn't supported) and uses the most specific matching user-agent group. Check the source for changes.
